analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (date bump plus a new paragraph on SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, SSDBlockIndex.oldest and oldestFirstSnapshot) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (one new table row at head line 375 describing active-store victim selection). The head_text unit for prefix-cache.md covers only lines 857-973, which are unchanged context. The changed hunk at lines 531-550 is visible only in the patch excerpt, which is truncated. No source code, crypto, key handling, TTL, disk budget, scope derivation, lookup tag derivation or routing-gate behavior is modified here.

The documented behavior relates to T-041 (SSD prefix cache) and its LRU/TTL and disk-budget mitigations. Eviction order is unchanged (last hit, then lexicographic tag). Documented safety properties are consistent with the existing posture: a closed store is never reopened and refuses removals, and file leases, epoch validation and the removal lock still govern retirement. On external-removal reconciliation the pass stops so the budget can recheck usage. Other refusals (unsafe root, lost or unreadable epoch record) do not end the pass, which is a bounded availability behavior, not a new attack surface.

Cross-file check: the base reference text still states TTL 1800 s and LRU across the whole kv3 root, so the new row does not contradict the T-041 sign-off. The new text implies concurrent schedules may pick different victims than strict LRU, which has no confidentiality impact.

Remaining questions for integration: the actual code changes in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDBlockIndex.swift are not in this batch, so whether the implementation matches these claims (for example, that closed-store refusal truly stops removals, and that snapshot exclusion of the first tag is correct) is unverified. These source files should be reviewed if they are part of this PR.
